briefs.title: Keep Claude Code’s cache warm for an hour
briefs.takeaway: API-key sessions and all subagents cache for 5 minutes. One setting makes it an hour.

snippets.intro: Needs Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

notes: `promptCacheTtl` covers the main conversation. `subagentPromptCacheTtl` covers subagents, compaction and other background requests.
On a Claude subscription, within your plan’s usage, the main conversation already gets a 1-hour cache. With an API key or a cloud provider it gets 5 minutes.
1-hour cache writes bill at 2x base input, against 1.25x for 5 minutes. It pays off when you often idle past five minutes.
Same thing as env vars: `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h`.

briefs.title: Run parallel agents without overwriting each other
briefs.takeaway: Two sessions in one folder share one working copy. Give each session its own worktree.

snippets.intro: `claude --worktree auth` creates `.claude/worktrees/auth/` on a new branch named `worktree-auth`.
Copies gitignored files into every new worktree:
Gives a subagent its own worktree every time:

notes: A subagent’s temporary worktree is removed automatically if it finishes without changes.
Add `.claude/worktrees/` to your `.gitignore`.
New worktrees branch from your default branch. Set `"worktree": {"baseRef": "head"}` in settings.json to branch from your current work instead.

briefs.title: Your Claude Code session isn't empty

briefs.title: Claude Code’s “Don’t ask again” writes a file
briefs.takeaway: Each “Yes, and don’t ask again” becomes an allow rule in `.claude/settings.local.json` at the repo root.

snippets.intro: Created the file by hand? Ignore it yourself:

notes: The rule applies to every session in the repo, including subdirectories and worktrees.
The first time Claude Code writes the file in a repo that doesn’t already ignore it, it adds `**/.claude/settings.local.json` to your global git excludes.
Rules are plain command text. Keep tokens out of commands you approve for good.
Run `/permissions` to see every rule and the settings file it came from.

briefs.title: A rule in CLAUDE.md isn’t a rule
briefs.takeaway: CLAUDE.md is context Claude tries to follow. A PreToolUse hook blocks the action, in every permission mode.

Save it and run `chmod +x` on it. Exit 2 blocks the call and sends your message to Claude.

notes: Exit 0 hands the call to the normal permission flow.
The script needs jq installed. Without it, it exits 0 and blocks nothing.
The grep matches that exact text only, so extend it for variants like `rm -fr`.
